A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LMLM research, despite the change from 'Large' to 'Limited' Memory Language Models. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original language-model pretraining, factual-precision and NLU evaluations, TOFU unlearning experiments, and retrieval and memorization analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds PopQA evaluation and selective-offloading experiments. Its separately attributed literature baseline scores are not the sole empirical evidence.

M1.justification: The core annotation pipeline, masked objective and retrieval procedure remain unchanged. v3 adds a selective-offloading variant for its new analysis, ranking facts by loss differences between STANDARD and LMLM and retaining selected lookup annotations. The main-text masking equation restates v2 Appendix A.3.

E1.justification: v3 adds evaluation on 1,399 long-tail PopQA queries concerning entities with fewer than 100 monthly Wikipedia views. This extends rare-entity coverage within factual completion; the existing Wikipedia, FactScore, T-REx, TOFU and five NLU benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: v3 Table 10 substantially expands the reported T-REx comparison to CoLAKE, K-Adapter, BERT-KNN, EaE, FILM and Toolformer, explicitly using scores from their original papers rather than matched reruns. The RAG backbone's relabeling as OPENAI/GPT2-355M is a clarification: v2 Appendix C already identifies that model.

E3.justification: New protocols include GPT-4 rewriting of PopQA questions into completion prompts, answer-presence scoring, and evaluation at six offloading ratios from 0% to 100%. The selection study first trains scoring models for one epoch. The previously documented training and evaluation settings are otherwise retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds a substantive investigation of how much knowledge to externalize: Figure 8 evaluates offloading ratios against NLU, perplexity and factual precision, while Figure 12 and Table 14 examine loss-difference distributions and selected facts. Existing database-removal, token-loss, entity-frequency and decoding analyses remain.

E5.justification: v3 Figure 8 adds error bars for NLU and perplexity in the offloading study, but does not define their meaning or associated run counts. This establishes added uncertainty reporting, not additional repeated runs. TOFU reporting retains the same conflicting three-run and five-run descriptions.

E6.justification: Original headline scores and numerical plots are retained, but v3 adds substantial results from PopQA, the offloading sweep and literature comparisons. New PopQA scores include 52.0% for GPT2-355M LMLM, 21.4% for STANDARD and 37.5% for RAG. T-REx Precision@1 results and some FactScore length/fact-count diagnostics disappear; several LLaMA diagnostics remain in Appendix D.3.

T1.justification: The autoregressive factorization, masked training objective and perplexity definitions are mathematically unchanged. v3 restates the loss in the main text and standardizes token-set notation in Appendix A.3; these do not introduce new theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: v2 motivates balancing internal common knowledge with external specific facts. v3 makes minimizing parametric factual knowledge and controlling application-specific knowledge scope central, newly asserting that factual information always requires lookups and out-of-scope access produces detectable failures. This substantially strengthens the controllability claim, beyond renaming the model.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations connecting large loss differences to difficult facts worth externalizing, and small differences to easy facts, contextual clues or noisy lookups. It concludes that greater offloading benefits the tested entity-triplet setting. Most earlier limitations concerning scale, retrieval errors, entity-only coverage and residual internal knowledge remain.

D1.justification: New reproducibility information describes PopQA filtering and rewriting, plus the offloading study's scoring models, five-token loss windows and numerical selection thresholds in Appendix B.3. Existing architecture tables, hyperparameters, annotation prompts, hardware information and the promised code/model release are retained.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning around memorization control, knowledge conflicts and explicit memory, including MemSinks and additional memory-based methods. New Tables 1 and 11 organize these distinctions. Earlier discussions and citations involving Rho-1 and SILO are removed; the change exceeds citation-style conversion.

P1.justification: The introduction and related-work narrative are extensively rewritten. Related work moves before the method, pretraining and inference are combined, unlearning precedes factual evaluation, and analysis is separated from discussion. The model name changes from Large to Limited, and an LLM-usage appendix is added.

P2.justification: v3 replaces Figure 1's knowledge-storage spectrum with a RAG/LMLM schematic, recolors Figures 2–3, and adds offloading plots and comparison tables. The main factual-results table is substantially restructured. Typography, float placement and display sizes also change, while most original numerical plots are reused.

improvement.justification: PopQA and the offloading sweep provide useful new evidence about rare-fact recall and a design trade-off left open in v2; clearer RAG labeling also improves assessment. These yield a modest net gain. However, the stronger absolute lookup-control claims exceed the retained fallback and residual-knowledge caveats, Table 10 does not establish matched comparison settings, and unexplained error bars and removed diagnostics limit the improvement.
